epic.title: Epic #418 wave 5 - bookend gates
epic.intent_and_why: Close the iterative-planning epic's own bookends: the role verifier must know where it is running from, the stop exit must not authorize a next wave, and the archive command text must resolve. Each is a check that today either cannot fail or fails for the wrong reason.

definition_of_done: All six issues are fixed, each behind a gate that fails closed when its tests were never written.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every gate closes on a -k selector keyed to a stated test naming contract; a zero-match selector exits 5 and fails the gate.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Targeted tests plus the coupled suite at each gate boundary; the full suite at g4.

hard_constraints: scripts/checklist_engine.py and tests/test_checklist_engine.py are crew 4's sole writers this wave
No hooks, no settings.json, no docs/agents/* doctrine promotion
Collateral red in a non-owned file is a float to the Admiral, not a local edit
fixed_decisions: A running process identifies an installed bundle by structure, not by name (launch-order pre-ruling 4)
The -k selectors are the cold critic's BLOCK remedy and are load-bearing, not stylistic

current_wave.objective: Fix the three bookend defects behind gates that cannot close vacuously
exit_criteria: guard_location, guard_mutation, stop_mutation and archive_c2b selectors each collect nonzero and pass
The full suite is green at g4

wave_evidence.claim: The structural predicate separates all three real locations.
wave_evidence.expected: Installed bundle accepted; main checkout and Commander worktree both not-installed.

Main checkout (C:/Programs/constellation-skills): no own SKILL.md, parent no CORPUS.json, 0 constellation-*/SKILL.md children -> False. Commander worktree (C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/epic418-w5-gates): the same three columns -> False.
wave_evidence.source: tests/test_iterative_planning_doctrine.py::GuardLocationStructureTests::test_guard_location_predicate_separates_the_three_real_locations, plus an on-disk measurement of the same three columns before crew dispatch

wave_evidence.claim: The guard is not a check that cannot fail.
wave_evidence.expected: An unconditionally-permissive guard drives the guard_location tests red.
wave_evidence.observed: Replacing _is_installed_bundle's body with `return True` gives 10 failed / 6 passed / 13 deselected, exit 1 -- red on the decoy test, on both non-installed rows of the matrix, and on four runtime resolution tests. The reviewer measured 9 failed independently before I added an eleventh test. Restored and confirmed by blob OID.
wave_evidence.source: Reviewer's own mutation run, and my own re-run after the post-review fix

wave_evidence.claim: The two-clause structural test does not self-certify.
wave_evidence.expected: A lone constellation-*-named directory carrying its own SKILL.md is NOT an installed bundle when nothing else marks its parent.
wave_evidence.observed: Found by the reviewer and fixed at g1-integrate: _is_skills_root globs constellation-* children of the PARENT, so the candidate satisfied clause 2 by being that child, and the test decayed to the old name test plus a SKILL.md. _is_installed_bundle now passes exclude=path. Removing the exclusion drives the new regression test red on assertFalse(_is_installed_bundle(lonely)) -- a behavioural red, not a signature error.

wave_evidence.expected: The flag beats an otherwise-resolvable root and is reachable from all three modes.
wave_evidence.observed: Passing, including test_guard_location_flag_beats_an_otherwise_resolvable_root and test_guard_location_flag_wins_and_is_reachable_from_all_three_modes. g4-integrate.c2 depends on this flag.

wave_evidence.claim: Both -k selectors collect a nonzero number of tests.
wave_evidence.expected: Nonzero collection, so neither gate closes vacuously.
wave_evidence.observed: guard_location 11 passed / 13 deselected, exit 0. guard_mutation 1 passed / 23 deselected, exit 0. Both run unpiped so the exit code is pytest's own. A bogus selector exits 5 on this machine, confirmed by the reviewer as a discriminating control.
